主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has charged Scott London, a former KPMG partner, and his friend Bryan Shaw with insider trading. London, who was in charge of KPMG's Pacific Southwest audit practice, allegedly provided Shaw with confidential information about five KPMG audit clients, enabling Shaw to make over $1.2 million in illicit profits. The two men met at a country club and became close friends and golfing partners. London allegedly provided the information to help Shaw overcome financial struggles after his family-run jewelry business faltered. In exchange, Shaw paid London at least $50,000 in cash and gave him an expensive Rolex watch and other gifts. The SEC alleges that London began providing Shaw with nonpublic information in October 2010 and continued for 18 months. Shaw traded on this information, making over $714,000 from trading on confidential data about Herbalife, Skechers, and Deckers. London also gained access to information about mergers involving RSC Holdings and Pacific Capital, allowing Shaw to profit from these transactions. The SEC's complaint charges London and Shaw with violations of Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5. The SEC seeks to order them to disgorge ill-gotten gains, pay interest, and face financial penalties. The case was brought by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). The SEC also acknowledged the assistance of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), Options Regulatory Surveillance Authority (ORSA), and Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE). The complaint was last reviewed or updated on May 22, 2013.
